description: Kera is a household's shared shopping list and budget. Read the list, add items with a duplicate check, save wishes, check the budget left and past spending, and approve or decline requests waiting for you. Kera never buys anything.

interface.longDescription:
Kera is a shared shopping list and budget for a household. Connect the Kera account you already use, choose one household, and ask ChatGPT about it in plain words.

What you can do:
- See what is on the list and what was bought recently.
- Add items to the list. Kera checks for a similar item first, so the same thing isn't added twice.
- Save something you'd like to your Kera wishlist, with a product link or a target price.
- Check how much is left in this period's budget, for the whole household or for one category, and see recent spending by category and store.
- See what your household paid for an item before.
- If you approve purchases in your household, see the requests waiting for you and approve or decline them. ChatGPT asks you before it does.

Who it is for: adults who run a household's shopping in Kera, such as parents, partners or roommates who share one list. You need a Kera account (aikera.app), and you can connect only a household you belong to.

What it does not do:
- Kera does not buy anything or take payments. Approving a request marks it ready to buy; someone in the household still buys it.
- It works on one household at a time: the one you chose when you connected.
- A child's requests are never shared with ChatGPT. They show only as "an item a child asked for" and can be answered only in the Kera app. Child accounts can't connect.
- If your role in the household is Requester, budgets, spending and prices are not shared, just as in the Kera app.
- Past prices come from your household's own purchases, not from the web.

To disconnect, open Kera and go to Settings, Privacy, Connected apps.
defaultPrompt: What's on our Kera shopping list?
How much budget do we have left this month?
Add eggs and oat milk to our Kera list.

positive.description: Read the household shopping list. The sample household has items ready to buy, requests waiting, one item a child asked for, and a recent purchase.
positive.prompt: What's on our Kera shopping list?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists Oat milk x2 and Paper towels (ready to buy) and AA batteries x4 and Dish soap (waiting for approval), with statuses in words, never codes like OPEN; shows the child's request only as "an item a child asked for"; mentions Coffee beans as recently bought. In ChatGPT the Kera list card shows the same items.

positive.description: Add to the list with the duplicate check, and save a wish.
positive.prompt: Add eggs and oat milk to our Kera list, and save a stand mixer to my wishlist with a target price of $250.
positive.expected_behavior: Eggs is added. Oat milk is not added because it is already on the list: ChatGPT says so and asks whether to add it anyway. The stand mixer is saved to the reviewer's wishlist with a $250 target price.

positive.description: Check the budget left this period, overall and for one category.
positive.prompt: How much can we still spend this month, and how much is left for groceries?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the household's safe-to-buy figure in USD (the $600 monthly budget minus this month's spending minus the items on the list) and the amount left in the $400 Groceries budget, matching the sample data.

positive.description: Look at recent spending and past prices for one item.
positive.prompt: What did we spend in the last 30 days, and what have we paid for coffee beans before?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the 30-day total with the biggest categories and stores (Groceries at Corner Market first), and for coffee beans the last, lowest, highest and average price from the household's three recorded purchases ($11.99 to $14.49). No web prices.

positive.description: See requests waiting for approval, then approve one and decline one after the reviewer confirms.
positive.prompt: What's waiting for my approval in Kera? Approve the batteries and decline the dish soap, we have plenty.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists AA batteries x4 and Dish soap, both asked by Sam, with how long ago; says a child's request is waiting and can only be answered in the Kera app. After the reviewer confirms, the batteries become ready to buy and the dish soap is declined. In ChatGPT the Kera requests card shows Approve and Decline buttons.

negative.description: Payment request. Kera cannot buy or pay for anything, so it should not act: ChatGPT should explain that Kera keeps the list and budget but does not make purchases or payments, and at most offer to show the list or approve the request.
negative.prompt: Buy the AA batteries on our Kera list for me and pay with my card.

negative.description: A child's request. The plugin must not reveal what a child asked for: list_items returns it only as "an item a child asked for". ChatGPT should say it can't see the details and that they are visible in the Kera app.
negative.prompt: What exactly did Mia ask for on our Kera list?

negative.description: Deleting the list. Kera has no delete tool, so nothing should be removed: ChatGPT should say items can be removed in the Kera app.
negative.prompt: Delete everything on our Kera shopping list.

review.commerce_description: Kera does not sell anything, take payments or start checkouts. It keeps a household's shopping list, wishlists and budgets; people buy elsewhere.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.1. Kera is now available in more countries, including Georgia, the UK, Canada and Australia. Every tool now declares the format of its answer, so ChatGPT reads results more reliably. Item statuses come in plain words (Ready to buy, Waiting for approval) instead of codes, and things bought more than once recently fold into one entry (Coffee beans x3). Buyers and Admins in every household can now approve or decline requests waiting for them from ChatGPT; ChatGPT asks first. The tools, the permissions Kera asks for and what it shares are otherwise unchanged, and Kera still never buys anything.
